knowledge-base.overview: Quarkus 3.x guardrails, CDI patterns, RESTEasy Reactive resources, Panache ORM, GraalVM native compatibility, configuration, and testing. Applies to Kubernetes-native microservices with Java 17+. Loaded automatically when agents work on Quarkus .java projects.

core-principles.principle: Designed for containers: fast startup, low memory, native compilation.
Live reload via Dev Services, Dev UI, and continuous testing in quarkus:dev.
Return Uni/Multi for reactive endpoints or plain types for blocking — both coexist.
Extensions process metadata at build time, not runtime — enables native compilation.
MicroProfile, Jakarta EE, Vert.x, SmallRye APIs under the hood.

guardrail.rule: Never mix blocking calls in reactive Uni/Multi pipelines without annotating the method with @Blocking. Blocking a Vert.x event loop thread causes starvation.
Use @WithTransaction on service methods that write, not on resource (controller) methods. Transaction scope must enclose the full business operation.
Never hardcode secrets or database credentials. Use ${ENV_VAR:default} placeholder syntax in application.properties and inject with @ConfigProperty.
Use RESTEasy Reactive (quarkus-resteasy-reactive), not classic RESTEasy. Return Uni/Multi for non-blocking I/O.
Set quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.generation=validate in production. Manage schema via Flyway — never rely on auto-DDL generation in production.
Use @RegisterForReflection only when reflection is truly required for native builds. Prefer compile-time alternatives (MapStruct, Panache).
Use profile-aware configuration: %dev. and %test. prefixes for development/test values, %prod. for production. Never use dev settings in prod.
Keep resource classes thin: validate input with @Valid, delegate to service, map response. No business logic in resources.
Test native builds regularly with ./mvnw verify -Pnative. Do not defer native compatibility until deployment.
Add OpenAPI annotations (@Operation, @APIResponse) on every endpoint and register health checks (@Liveness, @Readiness).

project-structure.description: Standard Quarkus project layout with CDI, Panache, DTOs, and Flyway.
project-structure.example: myproject/ ├── src/main/java/com/example/ │ ├── resource/ # JAX-RS endpoints (thin controllers) │ │ ├── UserResource.java │ │ └── AuthResource.java │ ├── service/ # Business logic + @WithTransaction │ │ └── UserService.java │ ├── repository/ # Panache repositories (optional with active record) │ │ └── UserRepository.java │ ├── entity/ # JPA entities extending PanacheEntity │ │ └── User.java │ ├── dto/ # Java records with Bean Validation │ │ ├── UserRequest.java │ │ └── UserResponse.java │ ├── mapper/ # MapStruct mappers (compile-time, CDI-scoped) │ │ └── UserMapper.java │ ├── exception/ # Domain exceptions + ExceptionMappers │ │ ├── ResourceNotFoundException.java │ │ └── ExceptionMappers.java │ └── health/ # MicroProfile Health checks │ └── DatabaseHealthCheck.java ├── src/main/resources/ │ ├── application.properties # Config with %dev. %test. %prod. prefixes │ └── db/migration/ # Flyway SQL migrations (V1__create_users.sql) ├── src/main/docker/ │ ├── Dockerfile.jvm │ └── Dockerfile.native └── src/test/java/com/example/ ├── resource/ # @QuarkusTest integration tests └── service/ # Unit tests with @InjectMock

notes.note: resource/: Thin REST endpoints; validation and response mapping only
service/: All business logic; transactional boundaries (@WithTransaction) here
entity/: JPA entities with Panache; keep domain logic minimal, push to service
mapper/: MapStruct with componentModel = "cdi" — compile-time, native-compatible

pattern.name: ApplicationScoped Service
pattern.description: Stateless service bean with @WithTransaction on write operations.

pattern.name: RESTEasy Reactive Resource
pattern.description: Thin JAX-RS resource: validate, delegate to service, return response.

pattern.name: Panache Entity (Active Record)
pattern.description: JPA entity with built-in CRUD and custom finder methods.

dto-pattern.description: Java records with Bean Validation annotations — immutable and native-compatible.

exception-handling.description: Register @Provider ExceptionMapper implementations for each domain exception type.

configuration.example:
quarkus.application.name=myproject quarkus.http.port=8080
# Reactive datasource quarkus.datasource.db-kind=postgresql quarkus.datasource.username=${DB_USERNAME:postgres} quarkus.datasource.password=${DB_PASSWORD:postgres} quarkus.datasource.reactive.url=vertx-reactive:postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb quarkus.datasource.jdbc.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb
# Hibernate — validate schema in all envs; Flyway manages DDL quarkus.hibernate-orm.database.generation=validate quarkus.flyway.migrate-at-start=true quarkus.flyway.locations=db/migration
# Dev Services (auto-provision postgres container in dev/test) %dev.quarkus.datasource.devservices.enabled=true %dev.quarkus.datasource.devservices.image-name=postgres:15-alpine
# Logging quarkus.log.level=INFO %prod.quarkus.log.console.json=true
# JWT mp.jwt.verify.publickey.location=publicKey.pem mp.jwt.verify.issuer=https://example.com
# OpenAPI / Health quarkus.smallrye-openapi.path=/api-docs quarkus.smallrye-health.root-path=/health

rules.rule: Use @QuarkusTest for integration tests — starts full CDI and HTTP stack
Use @InjectMock to mock CDI beans in integration tests
Use @TestSecurity(user, roles) to bypass JWT auth in tests
Use REST-assured for HTTP endpoint assertions
Test native builds with ./mvnw verify -Pnative on @NativeImageTest classes

quick-reference.item: ./mvnw quarkus:dev — live reload + Dev Services (no manual restarts)
@ApplicationScoped for stateless services; @RequestScoped only when per-request state needed
Return Uni/Multi for I/O; @Blocking annotation when JDBC needed in reactive context
@WithTransaction on service methods — not on resource methods
extend PanacheEntity for active record; implement PanacheRepository for complex queries
Avoid runtime reflection; test native regularly; use @RegisterForReflection only when necessary
@QuarkusTest full stack + REST-assured; @InjectMock for mocking; @TestSecurity for auth bypass
